subject: Post-call recap & pilot success criteria — SummitWorks POC
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@summitworks.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Jun 2028 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & proposed pilot acceptance criteria — SummitWorks POC

Thanks again for the time today — good alignment across product and infra. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth for the POC scope. Please confirm the success criteria and owners below or add/edit where needed.

High-level goal
- Validate Redwood inference end-to-end for SummitWorks' conversational assistant: accuracy for slot extraction, streaming latency under load, and predictable unit cost.

Proposed acceptance criteria (POC):
1) Accuracy: intent/slot F1 >= 0.85 on your baseline evaluation set (we can run the eval harness you shared).
2) Latency: 95th percentile token latency < 120ms for streaming responses at target concurrency.
3) Throughput: sustain 30 requests/sec (avg payload) with correct autoscaling behavior.
4) Security/compliance: no customer PII in logs for the trial; data retention = 30 days for sandbox.
5) Observability: per-route token and latency breakdown visible in Redwood Console; export link to shared dashboard.

Evaluation plan / timeline (proposed)
- Week 0 (this week): confirm success criteria and access (sandbox API key + test data).
- Week 1: SDK integration + routes mapped; basic end-to-end test (happy path).
- Week 2: Load validation and streaming verification; run eval harness and collect metrics.
- Week 3: Acceptance review and sign-off; handoff to trial operations.

Owners (suggested)
- Redwood implementation lead: Ben Carter (ben.carter@redwood.com) — SDK & API routing, streaming tests.
- Redwood commercial lead: Marissa Cole (marissa.cole@redwood.com) — deal/renewal owner.
- SummitWorks technical lead: Alex Chen (alex.chen@summitworks.com) — test data and environment access.

Asks for SummitWorks (please confirm):
- Confirm acceptance criteria above or propose edits.
- Provide sandbox service account / API key and a small evaluation dataset (anonymized).
- Confirm compliance constraints (PII policy, retention).

Attachments: POC-scopes-v1.pdf (high-level scope & constraints).

Next steps: if you confirm, I'll schedule a 60-minute tech sync with Ben and your engineering lead (link in my next email).

Thanks,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@summitworks.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@summitworks.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Jun 2028 17:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed pilot acceptance criteria — SummitWorks POC

Thanks Tessa — appreciate the clear write-up. Confirming most of this and adding a couple items from our side. Inline below.

> Proposed acceptance criteria (POC):
> 1) Accuracy: intent/slot F1 >= 0.85 on your baseline evaluation set (we can run the eval harness you shared).
We can provide the eval set — 6k utterances across our 12 intents. F1 target sounds reasonable.

> 2) Latency: 95th percentile token latency < 120ms for streaming responses at target concurrency.
Agree on the p95 target. One nuance: some long-form tool calls will increase tail latency — we'd like guidance on a fallback behavior if token budget is exceeded.

> 3) Throughput: sustain 30 requests/sec (avg payload) with correct autoscaling behavior.
Confirming 30 req/s is our target for the pilot burst. We'll also test a sustained 10 req/s background load.

> 4) Security/compliance: no customer PII in logs for the trial; data retention = 30 days for sandbox.
Strong requirement — we cannot have PII leave our environment. Please confirm whether Redwood supports disabling logging at the route level or redaction hooks.

Additional items from SummitWorks:
- Throughput SLA: if autoscale latency degrades beyond p95=200ms under the 30 req/s burst, we want an immediate fallback to a lower-cost variant with graceful degradation.
- Tool-calling test: we need to verify a simple tool-calling flow (invoke company lookup API) from within streaming responses so our agents can fetch live metadata.

We are good to proceed; please send the tech sync invite. Also attaching a short doc with our scoring rubric and internal acceptance spreadsheet (Priya will share the spreadsheet later today).

—Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Product, SummitWorks
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@summitworks.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 06 Jun 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call recap & proposed pilot acceptance criteria — SummitWorks POC

Thanks Alex/Tessa — I'm happy to own the implementation. Quick technical plan and what we'll deliver for Week 1/2.

High-level integration plan (technical)
- Sandbox credentials: we'll provision a scoped API key tied to your sandbox project (no logs persisted by default — see note below).
- SDKs: Node + Python SDK snippets; we will provide a streaming client example that demonstrates chunked partial responses and tool-calling hooks.
- API routes: map your assistant routes to Redwood endpoints: /v1/generate (stream), /v1/embeddings (batch), /v1/tool-callback (webhook).
- Auth: bearer token + optional mTLS for private deployments; for sandbox we'll use short-lived bearer tokens.
- Fallbacks: we will implement a model-variant fallback policy (e.g., gpt-lite variant) triggered when p95 latency > 200ms. This will return a degraded response but maintain structured tool-call behavior.

Streaming and tool-calls
- We'll ship an example showing: start stream -> partial tokens -> invoke tool-callback -> resume stream with tool results. That will be in sdk-integration-snippets.md.

Logging & PII
- We can disable request/response logging for the trial routes. For analytics we can provide aggregated metrics only (no raw transcripts) unless you request otherwise in writing.

Operational tests (Week 2)
- Load harness: we'll run a 30 req/s burst with variable payloads.
- Eval harness: run your 6k utterance set to compute F1.

Deliverables attached: sdk-integration-snippets.md (examples + curl samples).

I'll propose a tech sync for Thursday; Tessa will send the calendar.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Priya Rao <priya.rao@summitworks.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@summitworks.com>
Date: Wed, 06 Jun 2028 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed pilot acceptance criteria — SummitWorks POC

Thanks — attached is our internal acceptance spreadsheet (SW-poc-success-criteria.xlsx). A couple clarifying notes from product ops:
- We'll flag any utterances with PII before sending the eval set. SummitWorks policy: PII must never be persisted outside our control. We require a signed addendum if any logs are to be stored beyond 30 days.
- For the tool-calling test we will provide a stubbed company-lookup endpoint that returns JSON. Please include a small test that shows the assistant calling out-of-band and merging results back into the stream.

Link to our POC checklist: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3cSW-poc-specs

Attachment: SW-poc-success-criteria.xlsx (spreadsheet with pass/fail columns).

Priya Rao
Product Operations, SummitWorks

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed pilot acceptance criteria — SummitWorks POC

Great — thanks everyone for the quick turnaround. Summary of agreed items and owners below (so we can close the loop):

Agreed success criteria:
- Intent/slot F1 >= 0.85 on SummitWorks eval set (Alex/Priya to provide sanitized set).
- Streaming p95 < 120ms for standard responses; fall back to variant if p95 > 200ms under 30 req/s burst.
- Throughput: sustain 30 req/s burst, sustained 10 req/s background.
- No PII persisted; logs disabled for trial routes; aggregated metrics only.

Owners & immediate next steps:
- Ben Carter (Implementation): prepare SDK snippets, streaming + tool-call example, provision sandbox API key. Deliverable by EOD Friday.
- Alex Chen (SummitWorks): share sanitized eval set + stubbed tool endpoint by Thursday EOD.
- Priya Rao (SummitWorks): confirm acceptance spreadsheet and retention addendum ask — shared.
- Marissa Cole (Commercial): will prepare commercial terms for a pilot (monthly commitment & trial pricing).
- Karthik Iyer (Redwood): will join tech sync to review routing/fallback policy and observability hooks.

Tech sync: Thu 2028-06-08 10:00 AM PT — calendar invite sent (Zoom link in invite). Please flag any conflicts.

If that looks good I'll mark the POC kickoff as confirmed and Ben will start the sandbox provisioning.

Thanks,
Tessa
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
